heading: Application for Technology Risk & Controls Assurance Analyst
salutation: Dear Moore Kingston Smith Recruitment Team,
paragraphs: I am applying for the Technology Risk & Controls Assurance Analyst role because it sits exactly where I want to build a career: the point where technology, control and evidence meet. Moore Kingston Smith offers structured TRCA training alongside supervised client delivery and support towards the CISA qualification, and that combination - learning an audit methodology properly while applying it to real clients - is precisely what I am looking for at this stage.

My MSc in Information Security from Royal Holloway, awarded with Merit, included security management with an ISO 27001 focus, alongside digital forensics and network security. I also hold CompTIA Security+ and ISC2 Certified in Cybersecurity. That gives me the vocabulary this work runs on: what a control is meant to achieve, what evidence shows it is actually operating, and why the gap between the two is where findings come from.

My current work has already given me the discipline the role depends on. As an IT Support Assistant I administer access requests in on-premises Active Directory - confirming that approval exists before granting anything, limiting permissions to exactly what was requested, and recording each access period. That is the access-management side of ITGC work, performed manually and documented every single time. My own testing is equally methodical: on one project I ran over 150 manual test cases to 93.7% accuracy, deliberately checking for false positives and recording each result, because a control that flags something it should not is as much a finding as one that misses something.

At Co-op, as Person in Charge, my assurance work is control-based rather than system-based: weekly risk assessments and daily compliance checks against operational controls, reviewing the evidence, recording what I find, and raising whatever needs corrective action. I escalate through internal reporting and follow issues until they close, and I do it while coordinating a team of seven or eight and explaining control requirements to colleagues who have no particular reason to care about them. Working with people who are busy and would rather not be answering questions is most of what evidence-gathering is, and it is the part of the job I am comfortable with.

What I would bring is attention to detail, a methodical approach and a genuine appetite for the qualification. I am committed to preparing for, sitting and passing the CISA exam within the expected timeframe, and I would welcome the structure of the TRCA training rather than resenting it. I am at the start of my career and I want to learn assurance properly, from people who do it to a professional standard.
